## 1. Freeze an actual nonnegative C∞ test

Choose width \(\ell=1/10000\), \(h=49\ell/100\), \(\varepsilon=\ell/100\), triangle \(b_h(x)=(1-|x|/h)_+\), and normalized even C∞ mollifier \(\rho_\varepsilon(x)=Z_\varepsilon^{-1}\exp[-1/(1-(x/\varepsilon)^2)]\) on \(|x|<\varepsilon\) and zero otherwise. Set \(\boxed{\phi=b_h*\rho_\varepsilon}\). It is fixed, real, nonnegative, nonzero, C∞, symmetric, supported in \([-\ell/2,\ell/2]\). Fix support radius \(a=2\), \(d=\log3\), and translate four copies to centers \((-3d/2,-d/2,d/2,3d/2)\subset(-2,2)\). In the T1B notation, \(s=4/\sqrt3\), \(e_0=\phi_0-s\phi_1+\phi_2\), \(e_1=\phi_1-s\phi_2+\phi_3\); their complex span \(E\) is exactly two-Mellin-pole-null. Only the prime-power sample shifts \(3,9,27\) are active on this family. For the semilocal trace use a place set containing infinity and all primes \(p\le e^4\) (up through 53).

## 2. Exact mass and derivative inequalities

Write \(J=\|\phi\|_2^2\). Young's convolution inequality yields \(J\le \|b_h\|_2^2=2h/3\) and \(\|\phi'\|_2^2\le\|b_h'\|_2^2=2/h\). Since the mollifier is supported in \([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\), \(\phi(x)\ge1-(|x|+\varepsilon)/h\) on \(|x|\le h-\varepsilon\); integrate its square for \(J\ge(2h/3)(1-\varepsilon/h)^3\). Therefore \(\boxed{(18432/60025)\ell\le J\le(49/150)\ell,\quad\ell^2\|\phi'\|_2^2/J\le30625/2304}\). Outward decimal bound: \(J\in[0.000030707205,0.000032666667]\).

## 3. Rigorous complete Gamma diagonal

Let \(R(t)=(\phi*\widetilde\phi)(t)/J\). Then \(0\le R\le1\), \(R(t)=0\) for \(|t|\ge\ell\), and \(1-R(t)=\|\phi(\cdot+t)-\phi\|_2^2/(2J)\le t^2\|\phi'\|_2^2/(2J)\). Put \(w(t)=e^{-t/2}/(1-e^{-2t})\), \(C_\Gamma=\log(4\pi)+\gamma\). The full signed Weil Gamma diagonal is \(\displaystyle g_0/J=-C_\Gamma+2\int_0^\infty(e^{-t/2}-R(t))w(t)dt\). The tail \(2\int_\ell^\infty e^{-t/2}w(t)dt=\log\coth(\ell/2)\) is elementary. On \(0<t<\ell\), \(w(t)\le1/t\) and \(2(1-e^{-t/2})w(t)\le1\); thus the remaining correction lies between \(-\ell\) and \(\ell^2\|\phi'\|_2^2/(2J)\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\log\coth(\ell/2)-C_\Gamma-\ell
\ \le\ g_0/J\
\le\log\coth(\ell/2)-C_\Gamma+30625/4608.}
\]
All constants were bounded with exact rational Taylor/alternating-series remainders: Machin arctangent formula for \(\pi\), atanh geometric-tail bounds for logarithms, and \(H_n-\log n-1/(2n)<\gamma<H_n-\log n-1/(2(n+1))\) at \(n=1000\). Also \(0\le\log\coth(\ell/2)-\log(2/\ell)\le\ell^2/4\).
**Validated outward intervals:** \(\boxed{g_0/J\in[6.79514722,13.44129808],\quad g_0\in[0.000208659981,0.000439082404]}\).

## 4. Complete off-diagonal Gamma A1,A2,A3 bounds

For \(k=1,2,3\), \(A_k=\iint\phi(x)\phi(y)w(kd+x-y)dxdy>0\). Because \(\int\phi=h\), \(J\le2h/3\), \((\int\phi)^2/J\ge3h/2\), and by Cauchy–Schwarz \((\int\phi)^2/J\le\ell\), monotonicity of \(w\) gives
\[
\boxed{(3h/2)w(kd+\ell)\le A_k/J\le\ell\,w(kd-\ell).}
\]
The endpoints are rigorously bounded with \(1+x\le e^x\le(1-x)^{-1}\) for \(0\le x<1\) and exact integer-square-root intervals for \(\sqrt3\).

## 5. Explicit two-dimensional generalized spectrum

The full original signed Weil numerator \(H\) and physical metric \(M\) are exactly those verified algebraically in T1B: \(H=\begin{psmallmatrix}Q&C\\C&Q\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(M=J\begin{psmallmatrix}22/3&-8\sqrt3/3\\-8\sqrt3/3&22/3\end{psmallmatrix}>0\). ## 6. Correlated splitting and normalized phase separation

The exact difference cancels the poorly constrained common diagonal:
\[
\mu_--\mu_+=\tfrac{10\sqrt3\log3+83a_1-64\sqrt3 a_2+33a_3}{73}.
\]
The pointwise Gamma monotonicity \(w(t+\log3)<w(t)/\sqrt3\), together with \(\phi\ge0\), gives \(a_2<a_1/\sqrt3\), so the difference is strictly greater than \((10\sqrt3\log3+19a_1+33a_3)/73\). Combining this correlated lower bound with rational interval upper estimates gives
\[
\boxed{\mu_--\mu_+\in[0.26068352,0.26070960].}
\]
For the normalized \(\beta=1,i,-1\) four-cell tests, the **smaller adjacent full-signed-Weil phase gap** is likewise rigorously enclosed in \(\boxed{[0.04824774,0.04825257]}\). This reflects a **restricted finite-dimensional** generalized pencil; the corresponding full operator may have different low spectral behavior.
